verdict: Avoid new gold-jewellery manufacturing exposure in Kolkata for now; lend only to organised, GST-clean, low-leverage units with gold-metal limits and monthly stock statements, and decline any havala-linked or cash-heavy borrower.
title: Kolkata gold jewellery manufacturing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business actually is
**A Kolkata gold unit buys bullion or scrap, converts it into chains, bangles and studded pieces, and sells to wholesalers and retailers in Bada Bazar and beyond.** Cash sits in inventory and in the gold itself, not in the factory. The ICRA reports describe the sector as working-capital intensive, with working capital intensity of 15-20% and rising with gold prices [10], and as fragmented with unorganised players squeezing margins [11]. Pricing power is thin: competition from unorganised players and peers limits pricing flexibility, and regulatory risk sits on top [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the inventory days and the gold-holding statement first; if the unit cannot show where the gold physically is, ask for the vault and karigar records before anything else. ## What has changed now
**The local signal is weak and the national money signal is tight.** West Bengal GST collections are -1.3% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, 7.4 pp slower [D], and electricity demand is +5.7% against India +9.5%, 3.8 pp slower [D]. India-wide bank credit is +33.0% YoY against output +3.8%, a gap of +29.2 pp [D], with repo at 5.5% and a tightening stance [D]. Locally, Bada Bazar gold and havala operators have been targeted by fraudsters, with Rs 50 lakh of fake notes recovered [1]. That is a local news report, not a peer result, and it matters: **cash-and-havala linkages are the single biggest credit risk in this trade.** If a borrower's receipts are largely cash or routed through non-bank channels, decline. ## Where the growth is
**Peer results show the organised end is growing fast even while the local trade is stressed.** Shanti Gold reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 658.93 crore, up 121.65% YoY, with PAT of Rs 51.93 crore [4], and Q3 FY26 revenue of Rs 636.93 crore against Rs 303.22 crore, up 110.06% [6]. Ashapuri reported PAT up 7.76% and EBITA margin at 8.78% [7]. Sky Gold notes 22 carat is still 70%-75% of sales while 18 carat is rising [5]. Pursue organised manufacturers supplying these chains: GST-registered, bank-routed sales, 18-22 carat mix, and a clean stock-and-receivables book. Avoid job-work karigars with no balance sheet and any unit whose sales are mostly cash. ## How to grow safely
**Structure against the gold, not the balance sheet.** Take gold-metal loans or gold-linked limits where possible, monthly stock statements, and a charge on inventory. Rating reports show the safe profile: NGJL at total debt/tangible net worth of 0.5 times and interest coverage of 4.0 times [9]. Take monthly GST returns, stock statements and bank statements every month. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch the gold and the cash, not the sales line.** If inventory days rise while sales are flat, the unit is holding gold it cannot sell; ask for the ageing. If GST turnover falls below bank credits, cash is leaking outside the books; stop enhancement. If the promoter's other entities show havala-type transactions, exit. Collect from customer the actual inventory days, karigar count and gold-holding split, as the sources do not give Kolkata-specific figures.
watch: GST turnover below bank credits for two months -> freeze limit enhancement and ask for sales register
Inventory days rising while sales flat -> ask for ageing and vault verification
Cash or non-bank receipts above 20% of turnover -> decline or exit
Havala or fraud linkage found -> exit immediately
